P0208.title: Attempt on Extremal arc-transitive walk parameters away from cycles
P0208.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Extremal arc-transitive walk parameters away from cycles explicit counterexample Result: For odd m>=5 the established wreath graph C_m[edgeless K2] is simple, connected,4-regular and arc-transitive on n=2m vertices. Its base projection is cycle walk. Exact hitting means are j*(m-j)+m between different fibers and2m between twins. Thus tau_star=2*floor(m^2/4)+2m, tau0=(m^2-1)/6+m, and tau2=1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)). The first two scale quadratically in n, and tau_star/(2*tau0) tends to3/2, refuting all three proposed bounds. Check: The invariant fiber-constant and fiber-antisymmetric subspaces give the full transition spectrum: cycle eigenvalues plus m zeros. Its fundamental trace agrees with the direct stationary hitting-time sum. Neighbor hitting equals2m-1=n-1 as required by the source lemma. Obstruction: Verify prior disposition of this1994 question: the graph construction is classical. The source typo and rate-one convention are explicit. No mathematical gap found by the author, but independent review and novelty remain pending.

P0208.title: Aldous-Fill Open Problem 7.27 (our id P0208): REFUTED - arc-transitive graphs excluding the n-cycles do not obey tau* = O(n log n)
P0208.body:
Aldous and Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Open Problem 7.27 (Chapter 7, p. 259) asks whether, over arc-transitive graphs excluding the n-cycles, tau* = O(n log n), tau2 = O(n) and tau*/(2 tau0) = 1 + o(1). Our result (id P0208, 2026-09-08): all three claims are FALSE. The counterexample is the lexicographic product C_m[Kbar_2] for odd m >= 5 - the m-cycle with every vertex split into two non-adjacent twins - which is connected, 4-regular, arc-transitive and not a cycle, on n = 2m vertices. With g(j) = j(m-j) + m the mean hitting time at cycle-distance j and 2m the twin hitting time: tau* = 2*floor(m^2/4) + 2m ~ n^2/8 (quadratic, not O(n log n)); tau2 = 1/(1 - cos(2 pi/m)) ~ n^2/(8 pi^2), because A(C_m[Kbar_2]) = A(C_m) tensor J_2 so the relaxation time is the m-cycle's own; and tau*/(2 tau0) tends to 3/2, not 1 + o(1). Verification, as the source words it: exact hitting times by linear algebra at m = 5, 7, 9, 11, 15, 21 (all five formulas exact at every size); arc-transitivity checked mechanically at m = 5, 7, 9 (the group generated by the rotation, one reflection and one fibre swap has order 2^m * 2m and its orbit of one arc is all 8m arcs); and a Lean file P0208.lean with nine theorems, no sorry, axioms propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound only. Not formalised: uniqueness of the solution of (I-P)h = 1 and the tensor eigenvalue computation, both standard and checked numerically. Prior art not cleared.
odd m >= 5

P0458.title: Attempt on The standardized degree law in growing bilateral preference graphs
P0458.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics Result: The packet uses the exact root (k+1)st order statistic X~Beta(k+1,n-k-1). Ignoring internal edges among the root preferred neighbors gives D0|X~Bin(k,1-q(X)), where q(X)=E[(X-T)+]/X and T~Beta(k,n-2k). The actual error satisfies E[(D0-D)^2/k]=O(k^2/n+k^5/n^2). Beta central limits and explicit moment controls then give (k-D)/sqrt(k)->g(Z), g(z)=phi(z)+z*Phi(z), with convergence of its first two moments. The variance constant is v=1/3+(sqrt(3)-2)/(2*pi), and the standardized degree limit is (1/sqrt(pi)-g(Z))/sqrt(v), which is non-Gaussian. Check: All 720 rank permutations on four vertices for k=1,2 satisfy D<=D0<=D+2J; degree means 3/5 and 8/5 agree with independent two-endpoint rank probabilities. The separate fixed-k EWT root mixture followed by a gamma limit yields the same g(Z). Exact conditioning, L2 comparison, uniform integrability and a polar calculation of v are detailed in the packet. Obstruction: Author-only partial candidate for the broader source question. No independent review, current-openness or novelty certificate, and no assertion for every k regime.

C0129.title: Attempt on Recurrence-transience criterion for excited random walks under stationary ergodic environments
C0129.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine the branching-process-with-migration proof and where i.i.d. is used. Result: The proof of Theorem 3.10 under (3.10) translates the walk into a branching process with migration whose offspring law at site k is determined by the cookie stack at k; under (IID) the branching process is homogeneous in space and the criterion delta > 1 is the criterion for the branching process to die out... under (SE) the process is a branching process in a stationary ergodic environment (BPRE with migration), whose survival criterion is governed by the Lyapunov exponent of the environment, i.e. by an ergodic average of log-means, not by the mean delta of the drift. So the natural (SE) analogue is NOT 'delta in [-1,1]' with delta = E sum_i (2 omega(0,i) - 1) but a criterion involving the annealed versus quenched growth rate of the associated BPRE; for i.i.d. environments the two coincide because the migration term is affine. I tested this on the simplest non-i.i.d. case: an environment alternating deterministically between two cookie stacks a and b (period 2, hence SE after a random shift): the branching process with migration is then periodic and its two-step transition is again a branching process with migration with delta_2 = delta_a + delta_b; the criterion becomes delta_a + delta_b > 2 for transience, i.e. the average delta > 1, consistent with the naive extension. For genuinely random ergodic environments a similar averaging holds if the migration is additive, which it is (the number of cookies eaten per visit adds). So the expected answer is YES for (SE) with the same delta, and the obstruction to a proof is that the branching-process comparison uses independence between the offspring at different sites when computing the extinction probability of the process with migration; with dependence one needs an ergodic theorem for the total progeny, available via the Kesten-Kozlov-Spitzer approach only for i.i.d.. Recorded: periodic environments satisfy the naive extension; the general (SE) case reduces to an ergodic total-progeny theorem for branching with migration in stationary environments. Key identity: Periodic two-stack environment: transient iff delta_a + delta_b > 2, i.e. the averaged delta criterion holds. Obstruction: Ergodic total-progeny theorem for branching processes with migration in stationary environments.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0129-recurrence-transience-criterion-for-excited-random-walks-under-station
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

P0087.title: Attempt on Forced network urn convergence and diffusion scaling
P0087.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Forced network urn convergence and diffusion scaling structural argument Result: A complete fixed-step classification follows. On any event Z_n->z, the update forces X_n to converge to a binary vector x and hence eventually equal it. The bounded martingale-difference strong law gives x=Qz. The update limit gives z=(r x+f p)/(r+f). A binary coordinate of Qz can equal0 or1 only when all its positive-weight predecessors have the same x-value and matching p-value. Irreducibility then forces x and p to be the all-zero or all-one vector. Conversely if p=0, the positive stationary vector pi gives E[pi.Z_n]=(1-f)^n E[pi.Z_0], and Markov plus Borel-Cantelli yields Z_n->0; p=1 follows by complementing. Check: The proof needs no conditional independence. The strong law follows from summable variances of martingale increments divided by n, then Kronecker. The maximum principle can also be checked by propagating the set of zero coordinates backwards through irreducibility. Obstruction: This resolves the fixed-step convergence subquestion under the stated assumptions, but not the whole diffusion question. Fast synchronization, an initial layer, and the covariance specification must be treated before a full solution label.

P0294.title: Attempt on Compute a first order bias correction for continuous workload mean field models
P0294.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit model calculation, comparison identities and remaining hypothesis obstruction Result: An exactly solvable continuous-state control model shows how covariance enters the correction. Let dX_i=(-a*X_i+b*M_N)dt+sigma*dB_i with a>b>=0 and independent Brownian motions. The empirical mean is an OU process of rate a-b and variance sigma^2/[2(a-b)N]. Orthogonal deviations have marginal variance sigma^2*(1-1/N)/(2a). Therefore E X_i^2=sigma^2/(2a)+(sigma^2/(2N))*(1/(a-b)-1/a), an exact first-order correction with no further error. Check: The orthogonal projection onto the constant vector and its complement diagonalizes the linear drift. Their independent Brownian projections give the two variances, and summing them reproduces the one-coordinate stationary variance directly from the Lyapunov equation. Obstruction: This classical Gaussian calculation is a baseline, not a solution for the least-workload PDMP. Its interaction involves routing minima and a reflecting or sticky empty boundary; the appropriate infinite-dimensional covariance and response equations must be derived and solved with certified truncation and tail error. The source empirical approximation lambda^2/[2(1-lambda)] is not asserted exact.

C0020.title: Attempt on Optimal exponent for the computational complexity of randomised algorithms for percolation crossings
C0020.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Lower-bound the complexity by the OSSS inequality with the sharp four-arm exponent and compare with the exploration-path algorithm. Result: The exploration algorithm reveals the pivotal-rich interface, of expected size n^{7/4+o(1)}, giving sigma <= 7/4. The lower bound 6/4 in the notes comes from Theorem VIII.6 (revealment times complexity). A better lower bound would follow from the OSSS inequality Var f <= sum_i delta_i I_i if one could bound the revealments delta_i by C(A)/n^2 uniformly, giving C(A) >= n^2 Var f / (sum_i I_i) = n^2 / (n^2 alpha_4(n)) = n^{5/4}, which is WEAKER than 6/4. So OSSS with the 4-arm exponent cannot beat 6/4; the 6/4 bound uses the stronger Theorem VIII.6. Improving the lower bound needs a new inequality between complexity and the spectral measure beyond the second Fourier level; I checked that the third-level analogue of OSSS (via the pivotal-triples) gives at best n^{6/4} again because three-pivotal points have density n^2 alpha_6... which is smaller. No improvement. Obstruction: Both OSSS-type bounds saturate at 6/4; closing the gap to 7/4 needs a genuinely new lower-bound technique.

C0074.title: Attempt on Scaling limit of random walk on the high-dimensional incipient infinite cluster
C0074.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the scaling limit of the IIC itself (C0077) plus a homogenisation of the walk on the limit tree. Result: If the IIC converges (as a measure-valued process indexed by intrinsic distance) to incipient infinite super-Brownian motion, then the walk on the IIC should converge to the Brownian motion on the associated continuum random tree embedded in R^d, time-changed by the IIC volume measure, i.e. to the 'Brownian motion on the ISE-type tree' with spatial displacement given by the embedding (the Ben Arous-Cabezas-Fribergh limit). The walk on the discrete tree structure of the IIC is a random walk on a graph that is tree-like at all scales in d > 6 (the number of cycles at scale r is bounded), so the spatial position is a Brownian motion time-changed by the intrinsic clock; the intrinsic clock converges by the tree scaling limit; the embedding of the tree in R^d is a branching random walk-type embedding whose limit is the ISE embedding. Each step is known for the branching random walk trace (BCF 2016) and the difficulty for the IIC is the dependence between the tree structure and the embedding (loops, self-intersections). The rigorous reduction: the walk's scaling limit follows from (i) the IIC tree scaling limit with its embedding, (ii) a resistance estimate showing the effective resistance across the IIC at intrinsic distance r is of order r (tree-like), which is known up to constants from Kozma-Nachmias-type estimates. So the problem is subsumed by C0077 plus a resistance-form convergence theorem (Croydon's framework), which needs the convergence of the IIC as a resistance metric space, a stronger statement than the measure-valued convergence in the source. Obstruction: Resistance-metric convergence of the IIC in d > 6 is not established.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0074-scaling-limit-of-random-walk-on-the-high-dimensional-incipient-infinit

C0116.title: Attempt on Deterministic (1+epsilon)-approximation of the cover time
C0116.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Examine whether the Gaussian free field characterisation can be made asymptotically exact. Result: DLP show t_cov ≍ |E| (E max GFF)^2; the later result of Ding (2012, 'Asymptotics of cover times via Gaussian free fields: bounded-degree graphs and general trees') gives asymptotic equality t_cov ~ |E| (E max eta)^2 for bounded-degree graphs when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, and Zhai (2018) proved the asymptotic formula for general graphs under the same condition. Given the asymptotic formula, a (1+eps) approximation of t_cov reduces to a (1+eps) approximation of E max of a Gaussian vector with given covariance (the Green function), which is a deterministic computational problem: computing E max of a Gaussian vector to within 1+eps is not known to be in deterministic polynomial time in general (the majorizing-measure/generic-chaining bounds are only within constants; exact computation of Gaussian maxima expectations is #P-hard in some formulations). So the question reduces, for graphs with t_cov/t_hit -> infinity, to the deterministic approximability of E max of a Gaussian vector with a graph-Laplacian covariance; a positive answer would follow from a deterministic FPTAS for Gaussian expected maxima on such covariances, which is open; graphs with t_cov ≍ t_hit (e.g. cycles, where the cover time is dominated by hitting times) need a separate treatment and are the easier case since hitting times are computable exactly. Reduction recorded. Key identity: t_cov ~ |E| (E max GFF)^2 when t_cov/t_hit -> infinity (Ding; Zhai), so (1+eps)-approximation reduces to approximating a Gaussian expected maximum. Obstruction: No deterministic (1+eps) algorithm for Gaussian expected maxima with general covariance.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0116-deterministic-1-epsilon-approximation-of-the-cover-time

P0007.title: Attempt on Unbounded mirror component trapping every ray
P0007.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Attempted reduction to straight visibility Result: An unbounded unobstructed straight ray from the origin immediately rules out the proposed all-directions trapped configuration. However an unbounded connected planar open set need not contain any unbounded straight ray: a sufficiently narrow unbounded spiral corridor is a topological counterexample to that inference. Check: The corridor is only a counterexample to the topological inference. It is not asserted to be a configuration of the source mirror model. Obstruction: Unboundedness of the vacant component gives a continuous route, not a realizable billiard route. No mirror configuration trapping all angles, or theorem preventing one, was constructed.

P0034.title: Attempt on Recurrence of the planar horizontal-new vertical-old walk
P0034.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Martingale estimates for the axis-switching walk Result: The axis of the next step is predictable from the past, while its sign is fair. Both coordinates are martingales, their cross quadratic covariation is zero, and E|X_n|^2=n. Bounded increments and Azuma give summable bounds for P(|X_n|>epsilon n), so X_n/n tends to zero almost surely. Check: The predictable quadratic variation of the horizontal coordinate counts first visits, and the vertical one counts repeat visits; their sum is exactly n. Obstruction: Zero speed and a diffusive second moment do not imply recurrence. The occupation-dependent balance of the two coordinate clocks remains uncontrolled.
